newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks in London firmer, high-techs sparkle.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks in London firmer, high-techs sparkle.

text.p: U.S. shares were mostly higher on Wednesday following the Federal Reserve's decision late Tuesday to leave its funds rate at current levels.
"The tone is pretty good this morning. The market isn't euphoric but is relieved that the Fed kept rates on hold," one dealer said.
"In a couple of weeks people will start worrying about higher rates but for now the Dow looks like it will set new highs."
Better-than-expected results from Dell Computer Corp lifted high-technology issues.
Dell, which reported first-quarter earnings of $1.08 a share versus $0.42 a share a year ago, was up $3 to $102-5/8.
Hewlett-Packard Co was up $1/2 to $53-3/8 while IBM Corp added $3/8 to $173-7/8.

Elsewhere, Boeing Co gained $3/4 to $100-3/4 after a report in the Wall Street Journal said Continental Airlines Inc CALa.N had tentatively agreed to buy 40 jets from the aircraft maker, valued at about $4 billion.
Continental was also expected to declare itself an exclusive customer of Boeing.
McDonalds Corp was a notable decliner, slipping $1/4 to $51 ahead of its annual meeting on Thursday.
"McDonalds may face a tough time from shareholders," one market maker said. "They are going to have to explain their marketing strategy and how they intend to improve earnings."
Technical analysts said the Dow, which has risen over 900 points or 14 percent since touching a 1997 closing low of 6,391 on April 11, was likely to push into uncharted territory in the short-term.
Chris Chaitow, analyst at Robert Fleming thinks the Dow could climb to around the 7,500-7,600 level before reaching a peak in late June.
"The technical picture is not bad on a short-term view," Chaitow said. "But the long-term pattern concerns us."
Chaitow believes the Dow will begin a six to nine month retreat by early July, a correction which will slice up to 1,500 points off the bellwether top-30 index.
A break below key Dow support levels of 7,100 and 6,850 would give a clear signal that a short-term top was in place, Chaitow said.

Robin Griffiths, chartist at HSBC James Capel is more optimistic about the outlook for U.S. blue chips, predicting a correction will not start before the Dow has peaked at around the 8,000 level sometime in October.

"The way to make a film is to start with an earthquake and work up to a climax, according to Cecil B De Mille. He could have been making a film about Wall Street," Griffiths said in his latest technical analysis review of the U.S. stock market.
The June S&P 500 contract was up 1.45 points to 846.00 by 1050 GMT while the June T-bond rose 8/32 to 110-3/32.
